summary: Open-source 3D building editor for architecture and construction that runs in the browser or locally, and lets AI agents edit models over MCP.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Pascal Editor is a local-first, MIT-licensed editor for architecture, engineering, construction and operations (AECO). You model sites, buildings, levels, walls, slabs, roofs, openings, rooms and furniture, bring in 3D scans as reference layers for scan-to-BIM work, and let an AI agent read, edit, validate and save the same scenes through its MCP server. It's built with React Three Fiber and WebGPU.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building modeling software is usually expensive and closed. Pascal is open, runs in a browser, and is designed to work with AI agents.
whoFor: Developers building AECO tools with agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free browser-based building editor with local storage, a self-host option, embeddable packages and first-class agent support.

overview: Run npx @pascal-app/cli editor to start a persistent local install. It starts the editor and an authenticated MCP service on free local ports and keeps projects in ~/.pascal/data/pascal.db.

To connect an agent, install the CLI globally and run pascal mcp setup claude (or set up Cursor, Codex or another MCP client). Local mode needs no account and uploads nothing; a hosted workspace needs an account and some operations use credits.
You can also self-host one container with SQLite, or embed the viewer or editor packages in a React app. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: One agent client per local service
